audio._subject: A3 D4 G4 F4 E4 B4 A4 D4 — two bars, D Dorian. Opens on the dominant so the answer must be tonal; carries 1:4:9 as tonic, opening fourth, and a compass of a ninth; holds the Dorian sixth on the downbeat of bar 2.
audio._countersubject: (two beats rest) E4 C4 D4 G4 F4 B3. The rests are structural: a countersubject cannot cover the subject head, because the head is the one part that differs in the answer. Invertible at the octave against both — checked by spex-fugue, not asserted.

scenes._note: THE SAME FILE as the `monolith` scene, on purpose. The screenplay asks for the monolith at the edge of frame in A2-S02, A3-S04 and A4-S01 -- three shots, in three acts, staged between 2.4 and 9.5 metres from the origin the real monolith stands on. A second bundle costs nine instances and makes the piece's only continuity object reachable by a transform track; a second .ldr would be nine placements that could disagree with the first nine, silently, for ever. The piece is a montage and not a simulation: this object is CARRIED, and the document says so here rather than implying it walked. Each shot places it with a two-key constant transform at a lateral offset computed from that shot's own field of view, so it sits AT the frame edge rather than merely near it.

shots.title: Der Punkt
shots.note: Black. One point, Terminalgrün, at frame centre, one device pixel; it pulses once, slowly. Fixed in every cut, because this frame must be byte-identical to the last frame of the piece — see DER KICK. There is no geometry in this shot at all: the point is a HUD element, which is why it can be one device pixel rather than one projected millimetre.

shots.title: Der Schwarm
shots.note: The point swells into a swarm — the existing point renderer, ~3000 points sampled from 3005.dat's real surface. It has no shape yet; it is a cloud. Camera pushes in. maxBars 7 and not more: rev 1 gave this 8 s and a formless swarm has no second beat.

shots.title: Die Überblendung
shots.note: The crossfade, and the centre of the piece. The swarm collapses onto the real mesh of a single 1x1 brick, Black. The edge lines arrive in ONE frame — hence easing 'step' on edgeOpacity, not a fade: legibility is a threshold event, a statistical cloud becoming a thing that can be counted. Then hold silence for one bar; voice 1 enters with the subject AFTER the image has landed, alone. Then the brick makes one full revolution at constant angular velocity — 'linear' is the direction, not laziness.

shots.title: Die Montage
shots.note: The assembly. Nine real parts (7x 3010.dat + 1x 3710.dat + 1x 2431.dat, Black) fly in from the scattered start and settle into ldraw-scenes/monolith.ldr, staggered by real build step. The scatter is NOT authored as keyframes: it descends from a per-placement splitmix seed, so the document declares the generator and its constants and the choreography (M63) produces the placements. Nine hand-written transform tracks would be nine numbers that could disagree with the model. Voice 2 enters with the tonal answer as the first part lands.

shots.title: Der Monolith steht
shots.note: The monolith stands. Camera orbits 180 degrees from low, the object filling ~80% of frame height. Hairline HUD, lower right. The key light rakes across the studs so the module count is countable — the HUD says nine, and the picture has to be able to say it too. maxBars 32: this is one of the shots the 60:00 cut lives in.

shots.title: Stonehenge erhebt sich
shots.note: Stonehenge rises behind the monolith, Steingrau, materialising from the ground up at a scale that reveals the monolith was small all along. Camera dollies back. Voice 4 enters; the exposition is complete in four voices. The caption dates the sarsens, lintels, mortices and tenons — c. 2500 BCE — NOT the c. 3000 BCE ditch, which is a different monument on the same ground.

shots.title: Der eine Stein
shots.note: The module becomes a container. The dome does not morph out of the brick, it is BUILT while the brick goes -- two dissolves crossing, not one shape becoming another, because the whole thesis is that the thing is re-assembled rather than transformed. MEASURED AND DECIDED, not left open: the monolith cannot be at the edge of THIS frame. At the dolly's end the camera stands 127 mm from a bulla about 80 mm across, in a 78 mm frame -- the dome overfills it and there is no edge left to put anything at. Putting the monolith here means re-framing an approved shot, which is a bigger change than the note it would satisfy. The continuity object is carried in A4-S01 instead, where it works.

shots.title: Die Bulla bricht

payload.text: Ein Konto, das man nicht ändern kann, ohne es zu zerbrechen.

shots.note: The tokens arrive one per beat and then keep arriving past what the row can hold -- the camera pulls back and they still run out of frame. NO numeral and no HUD counter: tallying by object ceasing to scale is the actual historical reason the bulla was sealed, and it is an image rather than a caption on a caption. The linear dissolve ramp is what makes the arrival even, one token a beat, rather than eased into a flourish.

shots.title: Sardis
shots.note: The strike is on the beat and it is one event in three channels: the die lands, the bloom goes to 1.6 for a single key and comes back, and the marker cue is there for M71's binder to hang the audio accent on. The bloom keys are deliberately one frame apart at t=0.74/0.75 -- a ramp would read as an exposure drift, and this is a hammer.

shots.title: Die geschlagene Fläche

payload.text: Nicht die erste Münze. Die erste, die man nicht prüfen musste.

shots.note: Macro, rotating, chrome reflections off M56's synthetic environment -- the one place in the piece where the metal finish is the subject. The fugue reaches its first full cadence here, which is why the shot is short and the camera arc small: nothing should compete with the cadence. The caption is the corrected claim -- early electrum varied in its gold-to-silver ratio and could be manipulated; fungibility arrives with Kroisos's bimetallic reform, which is a better fact for this thesis than the one rev 1 had.

movements.title: Die Fuge
movements._note: Bars 37-57. The music for this act was already written: the plan has an INVERTED entry at bar 37, an episode, an entry AUGMENTED x2 at 43, a long episode, and the stretto at 53. The shot boundaries are those bar numbers and not a rhythm invented for the picture -- A3-S01 opens on the inversion, A3-S02 carries the augmented entry at its midpoint, and A3-S05 is the stretto. Positions are in millimetres with +Y up (1 LDU = 0.4 mm); the act occupies the world plate from x=7200 to x=9440 mm, which leaves Act IV the rest of the i16 instance range.

shots.title: Rom

payload.text: Rom · um 110 n. Chr. — das Modul mit Aktenzeichen.

shots.note: The screenplay offered two images here and rev 1 conflated them. This is the second: not the Pont du Gard (dry-laid limestone ashlar, no brick in it at all) but a Roman wall in opus mixtum -- grey stone facing courses with brick bonding courses running through them -- and, on the ground in front of it, a brick stamp. A standard module WITH AN AUDIT TRAIL is the thesis of this act, and it is what makes the three patent numbers in S02-S04 a continuation rather than a change of subject. The stamp reads COS, the abbreviation that dates a real Roman brick by consul, and it is enormously enlarged: at this scale a real stamp would be one stud, which is a stamp nobody can read. The camera descends from a wide framing of the wall onto the stamp, one dolly, one lookAt -- the wall is behind the stamp for the whole move rather than being cut away from. Voice 1 enters INVERTED on the first beat: the subject turned upside down, over a wall that is the same module turned into an industry.

shots.title: Batima

payload.text: Le Batima Soc. · Patent FR 588985, erteilt 1924

shots.note: The one genuinely great cut in the piece, and it is protected by being the only shock of its magnitude. Patentweiss is authored as a THREE-FRAME BLANK rather than as a background colour: exposure steps to 3.4 and back to the grade's own 0.7, bloom to 1.8 and back, both on 'step' -- a ramp would read as an exposure drift and this is a cut. The piece's ground stays black; the white is the flash and the brick. The block then turns once, at constant angular velocity, exactly as A1-S03's brick did -- the same shot at a different point in the argument. THE GEOMETRY IS NOW THE REAL OBJECT, from photographs of Stefan's own set: hollow studs with a bore through each, a body flatter than a brick, cast stone rather than plastic, and an underside of sockets. The camera looks DOWN on it at 26 mm rather than across at 14, because the bore in the stud is the whole difference and it cannot be seen edge-on. Exposure 0.22 rather than the 0.16 the white bricks want: 503 Very_Light_Grey is not colour 15. Voice 4 enters AUGMENTED at half speed on bar 43, which is t=0.5 of this shot: the subject stretched to twice its length under the first of the three patents. The patent number is FR 588985 and not BE 311029 / 1923, which could not be confirmed. THE LOWER THIRD NOW SAYS 'PATENT ... GRANTED 1924' RATHER THAN 'c. 1924', because the sources do not agree on the object's own date: architoys.net 1900-10, a PBA Galleries lot c. 1905, MoDIP c. 1930, the Belgian MOT 1900-1949. The patent year is the one date that is a fact. And there is a SECOND Batima -- wooden bricks with studs and tubes, introduced 1954 by Nazaire Beeusaert of Deinze -- which is not this object and must never end up in this caption. The reference is set as 'caption' rather than a lower third because 'caption' is one of the four HUD names with real layout; inventing a fifth would put text at an unstyled origin.

shots.title: Kiddicraft
shots.note: A rhyme, and a rhyme must be shorter than what it rhymes with -- three bars against four. Same part, same colour, same ground plane, same lighting; the camera widens by 36 mm to hold two bricks where it held one, and nothing else changes. The 'cutaway' that reveals the anti-stud is a transmission ramp on the second brick's material rather than a clipped section: the tubes are real geometry already inside the part, and making the shell glassy is the honest way to look through a thing this piece insists is real. Kiddicraft's brick and the 1949 one are colour 15 and the same part because they ARE the same object, which is the entire content of Interlego v Tyco. BATIMA IS NOT, and the photographs settle it: hollow studs into conical sockets, in cast stone. So the act now says something better than 'three of the same' -- 1924 is a different system that already had the idea, and 1940 and 1949 are one object twice. The rhyme is between the second and the third, which is also why this shot is the shorter one. 17 April 1940 is the filing date; 1939 is the date usually quoted and is the date of neither the filing nor the publication.

shots.title: Die Säule
shots.note: A third brick joins the two, then all three go and the column arrives -- a rebuild, not a morph, the same grammar A2-S02 used for the bulla, because the whole thesis is that things are re-assembled rather than transformed. THE COLUMN IS TUBELESS. `saeule.ldr` stacks three of `parts/brick-2x2-tubeless.dat`: studs on top, hollow underneath, nothing inside to grip them. It stands because it is stacked, not because it is clutched, and that is the reason the next shot exists. THE MONOLITH IS NOT HERE, AND THAT IS NOW A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. A second copy exists as the `begleiter` scene and was placed here -- 400 mm behind the column, 122 mm to the side, geometrically inside the 21.7-degree half-field. It is invisible anyway, and the reason is the exposure: this shot is stopped to 0.16 for a white brick, and Steingrau is linear 0.15. A stone object at that stop is black on black. The white-studio shots and the continuity object are incompatible requirements in one frame -- the same shape as PR #42's third finding about the monolith and Stonehenge. It is carried in A4-S01 instead, where the exposure runs 0.24 to 0.9 and it reads.

shots.title: Die Klemme
shots.note: THE CORRECTION, AND THE TITLE IMAGE. The tube inside the brick is the 1958 patent -- it is what made the clutch hold. Rev 3 put this macro under a 1949 lower third, which is a 1958 image with a pre-1958 caption and precisely the claim this act makes; splitting the shot in two fixes it and makes the argument stronger, because the clutch now ARRIVES rather than having always been there. The tubeless column dissolves and the official 3003 column takes its place -- a rebuild again, and the only difference between the two objects is the thing the shot is about. THE CLEARANCE IS AUTHORED AND SAYS SO: LDraw's stud outer diameter and tube inner diameter are both nominally 12 LDU, so in a correct model they interpenetrate exactly and nothing can be seen entering anything. klemme.ldr lifts the top brick 6 LDU (2.4 mm) and the transform track seats it, so the departure is a starting condition the shot resolves. At 28.6 mm from the joint with a 20-degree field of view the frame is 10 mm high and the gap is a quarter of it -- a framing that was impossible before the near plane started following the camera rather than the scene's diagonal.

shots.title: Die Vervielfältigung

payload.text: Interlego AG v Tyco Industries Inc · [1988] UKPC 3 — der Fall, der die Zeichnungen beendete.

shots.note: The stretto begins on bar 53, which is t=0 of this shot, and the four entries at t=0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 are the plan's own voices [3,2,1,0] one bar apart. That is the point of the shot: the visual multiplication and the contrapuntal multiplication are the same event, so they are the same four timestamps rather than two things that happen to look alike. The field is one Mosaic of 3600 modules with every eighth row and column in a second grey -- a white plane is a plane, and a ruled one is a grid, which is the shot's own word for what the column becomes. Four voices lighting four quarters of it is what M71's binder does with a voiceEntry cue's target. OPEN: 'marching outward' is currently a dissolve, which is a 3D-noise threshold and reads as materialising rather than as marching. A radial reveal keyed off distance from the column would be the true image and wants a track kind that does not exist yet.

movements.title: Der Token
movements._note: Bars 63-84. The plan's last three sections are here: a thirteen-bar episode on the countersubject tail from 63, the subject in the bass quantised to quarter length at 76, and a three-and-a-half-bar pedal from 80 into the final cadence at 83.5 — which is DER KICK. The pulse enters at 180 s and the final accent is at 238.571 s, which is exactly where the Kick's two beats begin, because `pulse.finalAccentAtSec` and a half-bar fixed shot at the end of a 240 s cut are the same instant by construction. Positions are in millimetres, +Y up; Act IV occupies 10000-11320 mm.

shots.title: Der Inkpour
shots.note: Everything on screen becomes its own swarm. The crossfade is the SAME mechanism A1-S03 used to make a swarm into a brick, run the other way — one pointCloud track per scene, staggered so the field goes before the column rather than with it. The pulse enters underneath at half time; `audio.pulse.enterAtSec` is 180 and this shot contains it. OPEN, and the same open item as A3-S04: the screenplay wants the monolith 'held in the background all along' dissolving here too. It stands at the origin, nine metres from this camera, and adding it to the scene list would load a bundle that renders nothing. It needs a near copy or the note needs retiring — and after three shots asking for it, a near copy is probably the answer.

shots.title: Der letzte Stein
shots.note: FIXED in every cut, like the Kick, and weight 0 — this shot is two bars at 4:00 and two bars at 60:00, because it is a held breath and a held breath does not scale. One brick, Terrakotta, alone in black, no camera move at all, going to points LAST of everything on screen. OPEN: the screenplay also asks for the colour to drain out of it before it goes. There is no colour track in this format — `material` can set opacity, roughness, metalness, emissiveIntensity, transmission and edgeOpacity, and none of those is hue — so the going-to-points carries the whole shot today. A drain would want either a per-scene tint uniform or a second bundle in grey to cross-dissolve to.

shots.title: Das Feld formt sich
shots.note: The points reorganise into a lattice, and the shot's whole job is to make 'neuronales Netz' and 'Noppenraster' the same picture — so it is rendered as an INVENTORY, counted, and not as science fiction. The caption is the recipe's own two numbers. The crossfade runs points-to-mesh, which is A1-S03's direction again: the piece's two legibility events are the first brick and the last field, and they are the same shot.

shots.title: Tokens

payload.text: 2017 — das Jahr, in dem das Modul die einzige Einheit wurde.

shots.note: The fugue's subject is in the bass here, quantised to a quarter of its length — same intervals, different century — and `audio.plan` puts that entry at bar 76, which is where this shot sits. No paper title on screen: it would date the day it renders, and subword tokenisation predates that paper anyway. OPEN: the screenplay asks for a glyph emitted by each node, travelling an edge, and absorbed. Nothing in this format can move a thing along an edge — there is no per-node emitter and no path — so what carries the shot today is three bloom pulses on the beat over the whole lattice. That is an accent, not a token, and it should be replaced rather than defended: the honest fix is a small emitter track kind that takes a target glob and a path, which does not exist.

shots.title: Sättigung
shots.note: The camera stops moving, and it is the only shot in the piece where that is the point rather than a consequence: everything else in Act IV is a move, so stillness under a rising bloom reads as saturation rather than as a pause. A pedal point in the bass under all four voices — `audio.plan` has it at bar 80 for three and a half bars, which is this shot exactly. The vignette opens as the bloom rises, so the frame gets brighter at the edges as well as the centre; that is what keeps it from reading as a spotlight.

shots.title: Der Kick
shots.note: Two beats, 1.429 s, `fixed` in every cut — 800 ms would be neither one beat nor two and could not be frame-exact against its own accent, and at 10000x zoom it is a flash where the collapse should be SEEN collapsing. The distance runs 690 mm to 6900 m, which is the screenplay's 10^4 stated as the two numbers rather than as a factor. The last thing on screen is the `seed-point` HUD element at 0.55, which is the value A1-S01's own track opens on: the closing frame is not a picture of the opening frame, it is the same element at the same value, so the loop closes on one device pixel rather than on one projected millimetre. `finalAccentAtSec` is 238.571 and a half-bar fixed shot at the end of a 240 s cut begins at 238.571 — the accent and the zoom are one event by construction and not by a number anybody typed twice.
